claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in nanoscale HEA multilayer coatings is governed by evolving interfacial dislocation networks.
Lattice misfit and local short-range order cause the proposed interfacial dislocation-network evolution.
Interfacial dislocation-network evolution mediates a gradual elastic-to-plastic transition.
The network enables controlled, distributed dislocation activity instead of abrupt shear banding or bulk diffusion.
The proposed test material is a nanoscale dual-phase HEA multilayer coating with coherent FCC/BCC or γ/γ′ interfaces.
The starting coating has inherent short-range chemical order and optimized moderate negative lattice misfit.
Creep testing should use sustained loading at a moderate temperature and under controlled stress or strain-rate conditions.
The test conditions should activate dislocation nucleation without causing wholesale phase transformation or loss of the multilayer architecture.
The evolving interfacial network includes immobile dislocation locks such as Lomer–Cottrell locks.
Interfacial dislocation-network density and configuration are sensitive to lattice misfit and short-range order.
Mismatch strain at coherent multilayer interfaces drives dislocation nucleation under sustained load.
The nucleated dislocations accumulate and interact to form a network that progressively accommodates plastic strain.
Moderate negative γ/γ′ lattice misfit improves creep resistance by enhancing interface stability.
Moderate negative lattice misfit stabilizes interfacial dislocation networks and enhances coherent barrier strength.
Misfit beyond an optimal range impairs phase stability and accelerates creep.
Relative to an excessive-misfit sample, an optimized moderate-negative-misfit sample will develop a denser, more coherent interfacial dislocation network.
Relative to an excessive-misfit sample, an optimized moderate-negative-misfit sample will have a lower steady-state creep rate.
Disrupting short-range order will destabilize interfacial structures and accelerate creep deformation.
The as-deposited baseline has uniform coherent interfaces and minimal pre-existing dislocation density.

Failure to observe both a lower creep rate and a denser coherent interfacial dislocation network in the optimized sample relative to the excessive-misfit sample would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
